# Select

Figma: [03d. Select](https://www.figma.com/design/a7Z956YZy9n6f9uz5DK16Y?node-id=69-899) · Family: 03 Form & Input · Status: stable · Version 2.0.0 · Updated 2026-05-22

A dropdown/picker form field. Looks like a bordered Input but ends in a trailing chevron - taps reveal a Dropdown Menu of options. The user picks one option; the chosen value displays in the field. Used for choosing from a closed list: deal categories, payment methods, contribution frequencies, regions, languages.

Reference image (every variant, labelled): `knowledge/examples/components/select/reference.png`

### Select Underline

A Select with only a bottom underline instead of a full border; same behavior and Dropdown Menu, lighter chrome for dense forms.

Level: organism · Contains: Input Label, Select Value, Input Helper Text

Use when:
- Dense settings or admin forms with many fields
- Forms already using Input Underline

Don't use when:
- Standard bordered forms: use Select
- Long lists that need typing: use Combobox Field with Combobox Menu
- Two to five options visible at once: use Radio Group

Accessibility: Announce it as a collapsed or expanded popup button, same as Select.

> Not published to the Figma library. Use it by name everywhere; in another Figma file take its published route or copy it from the Syntropy file (syntropy-components, unpublished.md).

### Select Value

The value atom inside a Select: placeholder or chosen value plus the trailing chevron.

Level: atom · Part of: Select, Select Underline

Use when:
- Inside Select and Select Underline (exposed so the shown text can be overridden)

Don't use when:
- Typed text values: use Input Value
- A complete picker field: use Select

Accessibility: The chevron rotation for the open state is runtime; expose expanded state in code.

### Dropdown Item

One option row in a dropdown list, with a check mark when selected. Shared by Select and Combobox so options look identical.

Level: atom · Part of: Dropdown Menu, Combobox Menu

Use when:
- Option rows inside Dropdown Menu or Combobox Menu
- A disabled option the user cannot pick: State=disabled

Don't use when:
- Action rows in an overflow menu: use MenuItem
- Search results with subtitles or icons: use Search Result Item
- Selectable rows on a full screen: use SelectRow

Accessibility: Expose as an option with selected state; selection must not rely on the green check alone.

### Dropdown Menu

The floating list of Dropdown Item options that opens from a Select (rendered in an overlay at runtime).

Level: organism · Contains: Dropdown Item

Use when:
- The open state of Select or Select Underline
- Simple single-choice lists anchored to a field

Don't use when:
- Overflow or action menus: use Menu
- Filtering by typing: use Combobox Menu
- Mobile pickers with many options or rich content: use BottomSheet

Accessibility: Move focus into the list on open, support arrow keys, and return focus to the Select on close.

### Select

A bordered picker field that opens a Dropdown Menu to choose one value from a closed list. Used for country, region, payment method, contribution frequency and language.

Level: organism · Contains: Input Label, Select Value, Input Helper Text

Use when:
- Choosing one value from a fixed list of about 6 or more options (country, payment method, frequency)
- KYC fields like employment status or income band
- Locked choices during processing: State=disabled

Don't use when:
- Long lists where typing helps (banks, cities, sectors): use Combobox Field with Combobox Menu
- Two to five options that fit on screen: use Radio Group
- Free text: use Input
- Picking dates: use Date Input
- Picking a Saudi region with chips: use ProvinceSelector

Accessibility: Required Selects left empty on submit show State=error with «يرجى اختيار خيار» in the helper, not only a toast.

> Not published to the Figma library. Use it by name everywhere; in another Figma file take its published route or copy it from the Syntropy file (syntropy-components, unpublished.md).

## Guide from the doc page

### Overview

Select is the standard form component for choosing one value from a fixed list. Visually it matches Input - same bordered field, same Label/Helper atoms, same sizes and states - but ends in a chevron-down icon that signals "tap to choose from a list" rather than "tap to type".

On Safqah, Select shows up on: country picker in registration, deal category filter, payment method selection, recurring contribution frequency ("Daily / Weekly / Monthly"), language toggle, and any field where the user picks from a closed, system-defined list of options.

### At a glance

### Atomic architecture

Select follows the same atomic pattern as Input. Two new atoms (Select Value, Dropdown Item) plus a new sibling organism (Dropdown Menu) handle the picker-specific UI. Label and Helper Text atoms are shared with the rest of the input family.

Atom - Select Value · 12 variants

Trailing chevron + value/placeholder text. Same horizontal pattern as Input Phone Value (which uses a chevron + country code). Variants: Size × State × Direction.

Atom - Dropdown Item · 24 variants

A single row inside the menu. Label + optional trailing check icon (visible only when selected). 4 states: default / hover / selected / disabled. Reused as instances inside Dropdown Menu.

Organism - Select · 30 variants

The bordered form field. Composes Label + bordered Field (with Select Value inside) + Helper. Looks like Input but with the trailing chevron. The Select Value instance is exposed - toggle its State prop to switch between placeholder and value display.

Organism - Dropdown Menu · 6 variants

The open menu container. Surface bg with border + drop shadow. Holds 5 Dropdown Item instances showing different states by default - override the Label prop on each instance to set real option text. Variants: Size × Direction.

### Sizes

Three sizes match Input conventions so Select sits next to Input fields in forms without visual mismatch. lg for primary forms, md for standard density, sm for compact dialogs.

Large (48dp field, font 16dp)

Primary forms - account creation, deal preferences, recurring contribution setup. Pairs with lg Input and lg Button.

Medium (40dp field, font 14dp)

Standard density - settings forms, profile edit. The most common choice for dense desktop forms.

Small (32dp field, font 14dp)

Table filters, compact dialogs. Use sparingly - fails WCAG 2.5.5 touch target on mobile.

### States

Five states mirror Input - same visual treatment for default, active, focus, error, and disabled. The Select Value inside switches between placeholder (no value) and value (option selected) based on the field state.

default

No selection yet. Placeholder "Select an option" in muted text, subtle gray border. The chevron signals "tap to pick".

active

Hover or pre-focus. Stronger border (border/strong). Same value display - only the field chrome shifts.

focus

Currently active, menu about to open. 2dp dark focus ring. The chevron may rotate 180° at runtime to indicate the menu is open (not shown in static variants).

error

Invalid or required-but-empty selection. Red border + red helper text. Selected value stays visible if any.

disabled

Inert. bg/disabled fill, muted text, chevron faded. Use when the choice is determined by another field or temporarily locked.

### Direction - LTR and RTL

Select flips correctly for Arabic. In LTR the chevron is on the trailing (right) edge, the value text aligns left. In RTL the chevron moves to the leading (right-as-visual-leading) edge, the value text aligns right. Same flip pattern as Input Phone.

LTR

Default. Chevron on right (trailing). Value text aligns left. Standard for English contexts.

RTL

Arabic context. Chevron on right but visually leading (since RTL flow runs right-to-left). Value text aligns right.

### Dropdown Menu - the open option list

When Select is tapped, the Dropdown Menu organism appears anchored below (or above, if there isn't room). It contains Dropdown Item instances - one per option. Tap an item to commit the selection, close the menu, and update the Select Value display.

The menu is a standalone organism - it can be composed under any anchor, not just Select. Same component works for filter menus, sort menus, and overflow menus inside cards.

LTR menu

Default. Labels align left, checks on the right edge of selected items. Hover state uses bg/brand/lightest-hover.

RTL menu

Arabic context. Labels align right, checks on the left edge of selected items. Same color tokens, mirrored layout.

### Dropdown Item states

default

Resting state. Transparent bg, dark text.

hover

Cursor/touch hover. Light green bg highlights the row.

selected

Currently chosen. Light green bg + bold label + green check icon on the trailing edge.

disabled

Option unavailable. Muted gray text, no hover response.

### Select Underline - alternate chrome

A sibling organism that swaps the full bordered Field for a single bottom underline. Same atomic composition (Label + Field + Value + Helper) - only the Field treatment changes. Use it on dense forms where the full surrounding border would create visual noise, or in contexts where the underline aesthetic better matches the surrounding UI (Material 2 look, classic database row editors, settings pages with subtle dividers).

Functionally identical to Select - same options, same Dropdown Menu, same accessibility semantics. The visual treatment is the only difference. Pick based on the surrounding form's density and visual character: dense forms with many fields benefit from underline (less visual noise); sparse forms with prominent fields benefit from the full bordered Select.

### Side-by-side comparison

Select (bordered)

Full container with Radius/8. Each field reads as a distinct enclosed object. Use for: sparse forms, hero fields, mobile-first contexts where users tap into discrete regions.

Select Underline

Bottom border only, no enclosing shape. Lighter visual weight. Use for: dense forms (settings, profile edit, multi-field configuration), inline editors, contexts matching Material 2 / classic database conventions.

### States - underline treatment

default

Subtle 1dp underline at border/default. No fill, no surrounding chrome.

active

Underline switches to border/strong on hover/pre-focus.

focus

Underline becomes 2dp at border/focus, signaling the active field.

error

1dp underline at border/error, paired with red helper text below.

disabled

Field opacity reduces to 50% - same underline color but visibly muted.

> **Tip:** Pair with Input Underline (page 03a) and Input Phone Underline if it exists. Mixing bordered + underline Selects in the same form creates visual inconsistency - pick one treatment per surface and stick with it.

> **Info:** Same Dropdown Menu attaches to both bordered Select and Select Underline. The menu doesn't care which trigger opened it - both organisms render the same option list when tapped.

### Code examples

How to consume Select in production Flutter code.

### Flutter - basic Select

```dart
// Standard Select with options
SafqahSelect<String>(
  label: 'Country',
  placeholder: 'Select a country',
  value: _selectedCountry,
  options: const [
    SafqahSelectOption(value: 'sa', label: 'Saudi Arabia'),
    SafqahSelectOption(value: 'ae', label: 'UAE'),
    SafqahSelectOption(value: 'bh', label: 'Bahrain'),
  ],
  onChanged: (value) {
    setState(() => _selectedCountry = value);
  },
)
```

### Flutter - Select with default value

```dart
// Select with pre-selected option
SafqahSelect<DealFrequency>(
  label: 'Contribution frequency',
  value: DealFrequency.monthly,  // pre-selected
  options: DealFrequency.values
      .map((f) => SafqahSelectOption(value: f, label: f.localizedName))
      .toList(),
  onChanged: (value) => _updateFrequency(value),
)
```

### Flutter - RTL Arabic context

```dart
// Arabic locale - Select flips automatically
Directionality(
  textDirection: TextDirection.rtl,
  child: SafqahSelect<String>(
    label: 'فئة الصفقة',  // "Deal category"
    placeholder: 'اختر فئة',  // "Select a category"
    value: _category,
    options: _categoryOptions,
    onChanged: _setCategory,
  ),
)
```

### Flutter - Select with error state

```dart
// Required Select with validation error
SafqahSelect<String>(
  label: 'Payment method',
  placeholder: 'Select a payment method',
  value: _paymentMethod,
  state: _paymentMethod == null
      ? SafqahSelectState.error
      : SafqahSelectState.defaultState,
  helperText: _paymentMethod == null
      ? 'Please select a payment method to continue'
      : null,
  options: _paymentMethods,
  onChanged: (v) => setState(() => _paymentMethod = v),
)
```

### Usage - Do and Don't

Four concrete Safqah scenarios paired with their wrong counterparts.

- **Do** · Choosing from a closed list: Use Select when the user picks one option from a fixed, system-defined list (countries, payment methods, frequencies). The chevron signals "tap to choose from a list".
- **Don't** · Choosing from a closed list: Don't use Select for free-form text entry. If the user can type any value (custom amount, recipient name, search query), use Input - typing into a Select is confusing.
- **Do** · Required field validation: On submit, mark unfilled required Selects with error state + helper text ("Please select an option"). User can see what they missed and fix it.
- **Don't** · Required field validation: Don't silently fail or only show a toast for required Select fields. The user won't know which field to fix and will hunt through the form.
- **Do** · Arabic - Nafath onboarding: RTL direction. Chevron on the leading (visually right) edge. Placeholder text aligned right. Matches Arabic reading flow throughout the Safqah app.
- **Don't** · Arabic - Nafath onboarding: Don't use LTR direction in Arabic contexts. The chevron sits on the wrong side, placeholder aligns wrong - breaks reading flow and feels foreign to Arabic users.
- **Do** · Locked selection during processing: Disabled state when the choice is determined by another action or temporarily locked (e.g. during async verification). Gray fill clearly signals "you can't change this right now".
- **Don't** · Locked selection during processing: Don't leave the field in active state while the choice is locked. User taps it, menu opens, but nothing happens on selection - confusing and feels broken.

### Notes from the maintainer

Implementation decisions, trade-offs, and things to watch out for.

> **Info:** Cross-page atom reuse - Select shares Input Label and Input Helper Text atoms with the Input family on page 03a. Means: if Input Label gets updated in v2.1 (e.g. a new "optional" indicator variant), Select inherits the change automatically. No duplication, single source of truth.

> **Info:** Select Value atom is exposed as a nested instance on every Select organism variant. That means props from the inner atom (Text, State, Direction) bubble up into the parent props panel - you can override the displayed value text per Select instance without unbinding the component.

> **Info:** Dropdown Menu and Select are SEPARATE organisms - not nested. In production code, the menu is rendered into an overlay layer (PopupRoute in Flutter, portal in React) anchored to the field. The component split mirrors that runtime structure: Select handles the field, Dropdown Menu handles the open list, and at runtime you compose them via the app's overlay system.

> **Warning:** Drop shadow on Dropdown Menu is an inline DROP_SHADOW effect (color 8% black, y=4, blur=12), NOT bound to a shadow effect style. If you adjust the shadow system globally, you'll need to update this inline value too. Flagged for cleanup when the Effect Styles system gets a proper "elevation/menu" style.

> **Info:** Chevron rotation at runtime - when the menu opens, the chevron should rotate 180° (pointing up) to signal the open state. This is NOT baked into the component variants (no "open chevron" state) - it's an animation handled at the app level. The static Focus variant shows the closed-state chevron.

> **Info:** Dropdown Item label text - when you build a real menu, override the Label prop on each item instance with the actual option text. The 5 default items inside each Dropdown Menu variant ("Option 1" through "Option 5") are just placeholders to demonstrate the state pattern.

> **Warning:** FONT WORKAROUND - Same as the rest of the input family: text uses IBM Plex Sans (Regular, Medium) since Font/Family/Base resolves to IBM Plex Sans Arabic which isn't installed in this file. Font/Size and Font/Line-Height ARE bound to font/size/N and font/line-height/N variables on every text node.
